instructions: Listen to the conversation before reading the transcript and answer independently. After submitting, check the transcript and reasons for any errors.
transcript:
Ava: We have arranged an evening exhibit for the community gallery. The tour begins at seven on Wednesday, not on Saturday.
Luis: Good. What will be in the first room?
Ava: A local artist has lent a portrait of her grandfather. The image is on a large canvas, and the frame is dark blue. She finished it last year.
Luis: I have seen her landscape of the harbor. Is that in the collection too?
Ava: No. The harbor picture is still at her home. For this display, she chose the portrait because it tells a family story.
Luis: What about the second room?
Ava: There is a sculpture made from clay and a small ceramic bowl. The person who made them has practiced pottery for four years. The sculpture is an animal, but it is not a statue of a real pet.
Luis: I have already written a note for the bowl, but I have not written the note for the sculpture yet. I will finish it tonight.
Ava: Thank you. We also have a colorful piece of fabric made by a textile group. The group uses an old craft in a modern style. They say each object can tell a story about culture without representing every person in a community.
Luis: Will a guide lead the tour?
Ava: Yes. The guide will speak for twenty minutes and then invite questions. Visitors may create a small drawing at the table, but they do not have to show it to anyone.
Luis: That sounds welcoming. Is the portrait for sale?
Ava: No. This is a free event, and the artist will take it home afterward. I hope people notice how different a familiar scene can look in another person's work.
Luis: I agree. A creative display can help neighbors talk about things they might otherwise pass without noticing.
